item.title: Nagasaki Kakuni: Braised Pork Belly — Guide
item.description: Buta no kakuni — ‘square-simmered pork’ — is one of Nagasaki’s signature dishes, richly reflecting the city’s Chinese culinary influence. Thick cubes of pork belly are simmered long and slow in a broth of soy sauce, sugar, sake and often ginger until the meat becomes meltingly tender and the fat turns silky and gelatinous, glazed in a glossy sweet-savoury sauce that dissolves on the tongue. A star of Nagasaki’s traditional Shippoku cuisine — a unique banquet style blending Japanese, Chinese and Western influences served on shared plates — kakuni is also enjoyed in more casual ways: tucked into a soft steamed bun as kakuni-manju, served over rice as a donburi, or as a rich set meal.
